subject: general
question: On 28 October 2025, the Union Cabinet approved the Terms of Reference for which commission responsible for recommending salaries and retirement benefits for central government employees?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8th Central Pay Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** of India officially approved the **Terms of Reference (ToR)** for the **8th Central Pay Commission** on **28 October 2025**.
 
• The primary mandate of the **8th Central Pay Commission** is to review, examine, and recommend changes to the existing **salary structure**, **allowances**, and **retirement benefits** for all **Central Government employees**, including the **Armed Forces** and **pensioners**.
 
• The recommendations are expected to benefit approximately **48 lakh active employees** and over **67 lakh pensioners** across the country, aiming to address the rising cost of living and inflation.
 
• As per the standard decadal cycle followed by the government, the implementation of the new pay structure recommended by the **8th Pay Commission** is likely to take effect from **January 1, 2026**.
 
• The commission is tasked with evolving a comprehensive framework that balances the financial needs of the employees with the **fiscal health** of the **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** The first Pay Commission in India was established in **1946**, chaired by **Srinivasa Varadachariar**. Since then, the government has traditionally constituted a new commission every **10 years** to revise the pay scales.
 
• **The 7th Central Pay Commission:** It was set up in **February 2014** under the chairmanship of **Justice Ashok Kumar Mathur**. Its recommendations were implemented with effect from **January 1, 2016**, introducing a **Fitment Factor** of **2.57** for basic pay calculation.
 
• **Composition of the Commission:** A typical Pay Commission is headed by a **Chairperson**, usually a retired **Judge of the Supreme Court** or a **High Court**, and includes **full-time members**, a **Member-Secretary**, and part-time members with expertise in economics and administration.
 
• **Purpose and Objective:** The commissions focus on ensuring that government compensation remains competitive and fair, taking into account the **Consumer Price Index (Industrial Workers)** and the general economic environment of the **nation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fitment Factor:** This is a crucial numerical value used to arrive at the new basic pay. For the **8th Pay Commission**, there is significant speculation and demand for an increased fitment factor to boost the **minimum wage**.
 
• **Scope of Coverage:** The recommendations of the **Pay Commission** apply to **Central Government** employees, **All India Services**, personnel of **Union Territories**, and the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.
 
• **Fiscal Impact:** The implementation of such commissions usually results in a significant increase in **government expenditure**, which is a major factor in the **Union Budget** planning and the management of the **fiscal deficit**.
 
• **Terms of Reference (ToR):** This document outlines the specific guidelines, limitations, and areas of study for the commission, serving as the **legal and administrative roadmap** for its functioning.
